item.description:
Beta 2: devices and artists. Sending to a device now looks at what is already there, copies only what is missing and asks once about albums that differ. PodBox iPods are recognised, get artist pictures and stop filling up with hidden Mac files. And every artist gets a page in the inspector: a portrait, who they are, a short bio and what your library holds of them, filled in quietly in the background and yours to edit. Beta 1 brought shell materials, the cover screen and the Pocket theme. 2.3.3 went out only as a release candidate, so everything listed under 2.3.3 below is new to stable users too. Betas are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Added
- **Pocket, a fourth built-in theme.** Handheld grey by day and console purple by night, with a moulded plastic shell, a grey LCD and its own logo. In the compact player and the mini player the album art sits in a pixel screen set into the case. - **Shell materials.** The Theme Editor's SHELL MATERIAL section offers Moulded Plastic, Brushed Metal, Bead-Blasted Metal and Carbon Weave beside Texture Grain, each with its own strength. A theme wears one at a time, and the mini player's glass wears it too. - **Cover screen.** The Theme Editor's COVER SCREEN section turns the album art in the compact player and the mini player into an LCD: LCD Grid lays a fine grid over the sharp picture, Pixel LCD redraws it in big square pixels, and Handheld LCD adds the soft colours of an old handheld screen. PIXEL SIZE picks how big the pixels are. A track with no art shows an unlit screen. The full player, the gallery and the inspector keep the plain picture. - **Sending to a device looks at what is already there.** Before anything is written, CrateDigger compares the albums you are sending with the device. Tracks it already has are skipped, missing tracks of a partly copied album are filled in beside the rest of it, and new albums go over as usual. This is the same for copy devices, converting devices and the offline queue with SYNC, and an MP3 you replace with a FLAC is recognised as the same track, not copied in beside it. - **An "Already on" sheet for albums that differ.** When an album on the device is a different quality, has different cover art or is another release of the same name, one sheet lists them side by side with what would be sent. Choose Replace, Keep both or Leave it for each album, or set them all at once. Nothing is chosen for you, and Cancel sends nothing. Albums you leave alone stop coming back; the sheet can show them again, and Preferences > Devices can forget them all. - **Folder Art is a switch.** Preferences > Devices has a Folder Art option for each device, and the Convert panel has a Folder Art row, so a cover.jpg beside the tracks can be combined with keeping, re-embedding or stripping the art inside the files. Rockbox iPods keep their old default (cover.jpg on, art inside the files stripped). Each device also remembers its own art setting. Ordinary conversions have the switch too, off by default. - The Devices screen's Artwork cell says when a cover.jpg is written as well as art inside the files. - **PodBox iPods are recognised.** When a device runs the PodBox firmware, Preferences > Devices shows which one (model, build and library layout), the Devices screen calls it a PodBox, and CrateDigger tells you what the iPod will make of your music: Mac files it reads as broken tracks, artist pictures switched off, a music folder it does not scan, the play log off, names it cannot match, paths that are too long, and compilations without an album artist. It only reads the iPod when it is plugged in. - **A folder layout PodBox reads well.** "PodBox recommended" names folders Artist / 2010 Album, which is how PodBox sorts albums, and leaves the year out for an album that has none. It is picked in Preferences > Devices for a new iPod profile; a layout you already use is never changed. - **Clean Up Mac Files.** Right-click a device or one of its folders, or use Preferences > Devices, to remove the hidden `._` files macOS leaves on an iPod's disk. Only files that are provably macOS metadata for a music, picture or playlist file are removed, a copy of each is kept on your Mac, and nothing happens until you confirm the count. A switch can also tidy the folders a transfer just wrote into; it is off until you turn it on. - **Next steps and Eject after a transfer.** The summary says what to do on the iPod (for PodBox: Update Database, Update Art Cache) and has an Eject key. The Devices screen reminds you to update the art cache until the iPod has. - **Artist pictures for PodBox.** The Artist Pictures sheet shows the artists on your iPod and writes a small square picture for those the iPod has none for, either in its Artwork/People folder or as folder.jpg in each artist's folder. Pictures come from your own files, an artist.jpg in your library, Deezer, or Wikimedia Commons (found through MusicBrainz), and are taken without asking only when your albums confirm the artist; anything unsure waits for your pick. Only the artist's name is sent. A picture you already have on the iPod is never replaced, and the ones CrateDigger added can be removed. Pictures after a transfer wait until you mark the check passed for that iPod. - **Artist pages.** Select an artist (or choose Show Artist on a track) and the inspector shows who they are: a portrait, where they are from, their years, members and genres, the opening of their Wikipedia article (with its credit and a link), and what your library holds of them, from albums and formats to plays and the tracks you play most. When two acts share a name, the page asks which one you mean instead of guessing. - **Artist info fills itself in.** A quiet background lookup finds each artist on MusicBrainz, Wikidata, Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons and Deezer, one at a time and the one you are looking at first. It never slows a FIX TAGS or artwork search you started, and it pauses while you scan, convert or copy to a device, when CrateDigger is hidden, on Low Power and offline. Only artist names are sent. Settings > Integrations > Look up artist info and photos turns it off; Look Up Again on an artist page still works. - **Edit an artist and their photos.** Edit Artist lets you correct any fact (what you type always wins over what was looked up), paste the right MusicBrainz artist, add as many photos as you like, and choose the one shown. The artist photo viewer pages through them, makes one the default, and shows where each came from.
### Changed
- **The iPod shows the artist's own photo.** The picture CrateDigger writes for an artist on a PodBox iPod is now the default photo on their artist page, so the two always agree. Picking a picture in Artist Pictures makes it the artist's photo too, and No Picture is now Don't Send to iPod, which keeps the photo in CrateDigger. A photo found for an artist CrateDigger is not sure of waits for you to pick it before it can reach the iPod. Pictures you had already chosen carry over the first time you open your library. - **MusicBrainz lookups share one speed limit.** Artwork search, FIX TAGS, DEEP SCAN, CD lookup and artist pictures wait their turn at the same gate instead of each keeping its own count, so using two together no longer gets refused by MusicBrainz. - **Carbon wears carbon weave** in place of its grain, and its selection lamp in the light theme now glows the same orange as the light it throws on the row. - **Llama '97 wears brushed metal.** - Themes you made that inherit from Carbon pick up the weave with it, even one that sets its own grain. To keep grain, open the theme in the Theme Editor, switch Texture Grain on and save.
### Fixed
- **Device transfers no longer leave half-written files.** Each file is written under a temporary name and moved into place when it is complete, so a failed or cancelled send keeps the old file, and an unplugged drive does not leave a track that stops halfway. - **Replacing an album never leaves it empty.** The new files are written first and the old ones removed only when every new file arrived. Cancel keeps the old files. - **Nothing is written or removed outside the device's music folder**, so backups and an iPod's own database are left alone. - **The device's contents stay up to date after a send.** The browser and the offline queue see what was just copied, replaced or removed without a rescan. Copy-mode devices no longer silently write "(2)" copies, and SYNC no longer converts a file more than once. - Cancel and the busy light now follow a device send, SYNC or conversion all the way to the end, including the final renames, deletions and cover files. - **Sending to a device no longer leaves hidden Mac files behind.** Files are copied without the extra information macOS adds on a FAT disk, which is what made `._` files that PodBox read as broken tracks, and the one `._` file macOS still makes for each file and folder CrateDigger writes (to hold a tag it cannot drop) is removed straight after. Converting devices convert on your Mac and copy the finished file over, so nothing is written to the device half-done. - **Every write to a device is checked first.** CrateDigger now writes to a device only in the places it is meant to (the music folder, covers beside it, artist pictures), never in the player's own folders, and replaces or removes only files it can show it wrote itself or that you chose to replace. A file you added is left alone and reported. A copy of anything replaced or removed is kept on your Mac. - **Names a FAT disk cannot hold are fixed on the way.** Folders and files with characters such as ? : or a trailing dot (R.E.M.) are written with the characters removed or replaced, so the album lands instead of failing.

Beta 1: themes get materials and screens. A theme can give the console a shell of moulded plastic, brushed metal, bead-blasted metal or carbon weave, and the compact player and the mini player can show the album art as a little LCD behind a recessed bezel, like a retro handheld. A new theme, Pocket, puts both together. 2.3.3 went out only as a release candidate, so everything listed under 2.3.3 below is new to stable users too. Betas are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.

Release Candidate 1: picking a track is instant again, folding into the compact player and back is a smooth blur, double-clicking the top edge of the window zooms it again, and the compact player always opens in the middle of the screen. Beta 1 made shuffle let go when you turn it off, kept the display's animation up when you switch desktops and turn down, and kept the compact player's artwork in place. Release candidates are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Added
- **Quick EQ moves between faders.** With a fader lit, the Left and Right arrows, or A and D, light the one beside it, so you can work across the whole equalizer from the keyboard. It stops at the first and last band.
### Changed
- **Folding into the compact player goes out of focus and back.** The console blurs, the window changes size, and the new view comes into focus already at its final size. The window no longer jumps part of the way or stutters when you unfold it. - **The compact player opens in the middle of the screen.** Folding into it already did; starting CrateDigger in the compact player now does too, wherever you last left it.
### Fixed
- **Selecting is instant again.** Clicking a track, an album or an artist, or moving with the arrow keys, could take most of a second to respond in a large library. - **Double-clicking the top edge of the window works again.** On macOS 27 it did nothing. It now zooms the window, or expands the compact player to the full console, following your Desktop & Dock setting. - **Turning shuffle off really turns it off.** Next and Previous kept following the shuffled order until you played something else. Turning shuffle off now puts what is playing back in its album, crate or playlist order, and turning it on shuffles everything still to come. The song playing carries on either way. - **The display's animation no longer freezes when you switch desktops.** Coming back to the desktop CrateDigger is on left the LED animation stuck on its last frame until the next song started. - **The animation follows the volume properly.** Turning the volume down a little made the bars drop almost to nothing. They now fall by as much as the sound does. - **Album art stays in its frame in the compact player.** A cover that is not perfectly square, or a YouTube thumbnail, spilled out of its frame and ran into the display. - **Quick EQ keeps hold of the fader you moved to.** Moving the pointer off the fader you first pointed at no longer lets go of the one the keys moved to, as long as it stays over the equalizer.
